[JEE Main 2021, 31 Aug (Shift 2)]
questions.explanation:
For first line of Lyman series, \(n_1=1, n_2=2\)
\[
\begin{aligned}
& \frac{1}{\lambda}=R\left(1-\frac{1}{4}\right)=\frac{3}{4} R \\
& \lambda=\frac{4}{3 R}
\end{aligned}
\]

For \(3^{\text {rd }}\) line of Paschen series, \(n_1=3, n_2=6\)
\[
\frac{1}{\lambda_3}=R\left(\frac{1}{3^2}-\frac{1}{6^2}\right)=\frac{R}{9} \times \frac{3}{4}
\]

For \(2^{\text {nd }}\) line of Balmer series, \(n_1=2, n_2=4\)
\[
\frac{1}{\lambda_2}=R\left(\frac{1}{2^2}-\frac{1}{4^2}\right)=\frac{R}{4} \times \frac{3}{4}
\]

Thus, \(a \lambda=\lambda_3-\lambda_2=\frac{12}{R}-\frac{16}{3 R}=\frac{20}{3 R}\)
\[
a\left(\frac{4}{3 R}\right)=\frac{20}{3 R} \Rightarrow a=5
\]

questions.question:
If for some \(p, q, r \in R\), not all have same sign, one of the roots of the equation \(\left(p^2+q^2\right) x^2-2 q(p+r) x+q^2+r^2=0\) is also a root of the equation \(x^2+2 x-8=0\), then \(\frac{q^2+r^2}{p^2}\) equal to _____ .

 

[JEE Main 2022, 26 Jul (Shift 1)]
questions.explanation:
The first equation is

\((p^2+q^2)x^2-2q(p+r)x+q^2+r^2=0\).

Rewrite its left-hand side as

\((px-q)^2+(qx-r)^2\).

Indeed, \((px-q)^2+(qx-r)^2\)

\(=p^2x^2-2pqx+q^2+q^2x^2-2qrx+r^2\)

\(=(p^2+q^2)x^2-2q(p+r)x+q^2+r^2\).

Let \(x\) be the common root.

Since all quantities are real and a sum of two squares is zero,

both squares must be zero.

Thus \(px-q=0\)

and \(qx-r=0\).

Therefore, \(q=px\)

and \(r=qx=px^2\).

The common root also satisfies

\(x^2+2x-8=0\).

Factorising, \((x-2)(x+4)=0\).

Hence \(x=2\) or \(x=-4\).

If \(x=2\), then \(q=2p\)

and \(r=4p\).

Thus \(p,q,r\) all have the same sign, which is not allowed.

Therefore, \(x=-4\).

Then \(q=-4p\)

and \(r=16p\).

Since the required expression contains \(p^2\), we have \(p\ne0\).

Hence \(\dfrac{q^2+r^2}{p^2}=\dfrac{(-4p)^2+(16p)^2}{p^2}\)

\(=\dfrac{16p^2+256p^2}{p^2}=272\).

Therefore, the required value is \(272\).

questions.question:
The number of distinct real roots of the equation x5x3−x2−x+1 +x3x3−4x2−2x+4−1=0 is

 

[JEE Main 2022, 26 Jul (Shift 1)]
questions.explanation:
First expand the given expression:

\(x^5(x^3-x^2-x+1)+x(3x^3-4x^2-2x+4)-1\)

\(=x^8-x^7-x^6+x^5+3x^4-4x^3-2x^2+4x-1\).

Substituting \(x=1\) gives \(0\), so \(x-1\) is a factor.

After dividing twice by \(x-1\), \(x=1\) is found to be a repeated root.

Substituting \(x=-1\) also gives \(0\), so \(x+1\) is a factor.

The complete factorisation is

\((x-1)^2(x+1)(x^5+3x-1)=0\).

Thus \(x=1\) and \(x=-1\) are two distinct real roots.

Now consider

\(g(x)=x^5+3x-1\).

Its derivative is

\(g'(x)=5x^4+3\).

Since

\(5x^4+3>0\)

for every real \(x\), \(g(x)\) is strictly increasing.

Therefore, \(g(x)=0\) can have at most one real root.

Also,

\(g(0)=-1<0\)

and

\(g(1)=3>0\).

Hence, by continuity, \(g(x)=0\) has exactly one real root in \((0,1)\).

This root is different from \(1\) and \(-1\).

Therefore, the original equation has \(3\) distinct real roots.

questions.question: The equations of the sides \( A B, B C \) and \( C A \) of a triangle \( A B C \) are \( 2 x+y=0, x+p y=15 a \) and \( x-y=3 \) respectively. If its orthocentre is \( (2, a), \frac{-1}{2}<a<2 \) , then \( p \) is equal to
questions.explanation:
The sides \(AB\) and \(CA\) are \(2x+y=0\) and \(x-y=3\), respectively.

Their intersection is vertex \(A\).

From \(2x+y=0\), we get \(y=-2x\).

Substituting in \(x-y=3\), we get \(3x=3\).

Therefore, \(A=(1,-2)\).

The slope of \(AB\) is \(-2\).

Hence the altitude from \(C\) has slope \(\dfrac{1}{2}\).

Since the orthocenter is \(H=(2,a)\), the altitude from \(C\) is \(y-a=\dfrac{1}{2}(x-2)\).

The point \(C\) also lies on \(x-y=3\).

Solving these two equations gives \(C=(4+2a,1+2a)\).

The slope of \(AH\) is \(\dfrac{a-(-2)}{2-1}=a+2\).

Since \(AH\) is perpendicular to \(BC\), the slope of \(BC\) is \(-\dfrac{1}{a+2}\).

The line \(BC\) is \(x+py=15a\), whose slope is \(-\dfrac{1}{p}\).

Therefore, \(p=a+2\).

Substituting \(C=(4+2a,1+2a)\) in \(x+py=15a\), we get \(4+2a+(a+2)(1+2a)=15a\).

Expanding, \(4+2a+2a^2+5a+2=15a\).

Thus \(2a^2-8a+6=0\).

Dividing by \(2\), \(a^2-4a+3=0\).

Factoring, \((a-1)(a-3)=0\).

Therefore, \(a=1\) or \(a=3\).

Given \(-\dfrac{1}{2}<a<2\), the valid value is \(a=1\).

Hence \(p=a+2=3\).

The intended answer is \(6\).
